option_relations.rationale: Familial progressive cardiac conduction defect is a disorder of the heart's electrical conduction system, leading to bradyarrhythmias and heart block. Catecholaminergic polymorphic ventricular tachycardia (CPVT) is a genetic disorder characterized by stress-induced ventricular arrhythmias. These are distinct conditions.

Idiopathic Complete Heart Block is a conduction abnormality where electrical signals from the atria do not reach the ventricles. Catecholaminergic polymorphic ventricular tachycardia (CPVT) is a disorder of ventricular arrhythmias triggered by adrenergic stimulation. They are different pathologies.

Coronary vasospasm (Prinzmetal's angina) is caused by transient narrowing of coronary arteries, leading to myocardial ischemia. Catecholaminergic polymorphic ventricular tachycardia (CPVT) is an electrical disorder of the heart. These are unrelated.

Coronary spasm with complete atrioventricular block involves vascular spasm and a conduction defect. Catecholaminergic polymorphic ventricular tachycardia (CPVT) is a primary electrical instability of the ventricles, distinct from coronary spasm or AV block.
